title: gpu-oom-debug-notes-anna-kim
content:
GPU OOM Debug Notes — Anna Kim

Context:
- Seeing intermittent GPU OOMs on prod-dedicated nodes (g4dn-like, 16GB) during batch scoring for long-context models (context ~12k tokens).
- Errors started after rolling a CUDA/cuDNN update on the Dedicated fleet (driver 535.x -> 560.x) and upgrading the runtime image (pytorch 2.2, cuda 12.1).
- A few customers reported failed requests with ~1-5% error rate under load spikes.
- Repro workload: batched inference with dynamic batching (max batch size 8), kv-cache enabled, sequence_len=12000 for a small subset of requests.

Reproduction steps I tried locally:
1) Pull prod-like image and run a single-worker container on g4dn.xlarge with 16GB GPU.
2) Serve a trimmed model (7B) converted to 4-bit quant on disk.
3) Run ab load: 50 concurrent requests, each with ~8k tokens prompt, request size ~25MB.

Commands and checks run (notes):
- nvidia-smi (before/after):
  - shows driver 560.49, CUDA Version: 12.1, GPU memory spikes to 99% briefly before OOM kill.
- dmesg | grep -i oom:
  - no system OOM, but kernel logs show "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1e): 79" around crashes (possible GPU fault).
- journalctl -u redwood-serving -f:
  - runtime printed Tensor allocation error: "CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.5 GiB (GPU 0; 15.90 GiB total capacity; 14.90 GiB already allocated)"
- python repro script run with torch.cuda.memory_summary(): captured peak_allocated and reserved numbers pre-crash.
- checked libcudnn and libcuda versions in container: ldconfig -p | grep cudnn -> cudnn 8.9, libcuda.so -> vendor driver 560 present.
- nvcc --version in image: shows 12.1, matches driver CUDA version (12.1) but the PyTorch binary was built for cuda 11.8 (checked torch.version.cuda = '11.8').

Error snippets collected:
- "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.20 GiB (GPU 0; 14.76 GiB total capacity; 13.84 GiB already allocated)"
- "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1e): 79, pid=1234, GPU has fallen off the bus"
- "cuDNN library not found or mismatch: libcudnn.so.8: version `CUDNN_8.7' not found"
- PyTorch warns on startup: "Warning: Torch compiled with CUDA 11.8 but detected CUDA runtime 12.1. This might cause undefined behavior."

Hypotheses / observations:
- Hypothesis A: PyTorch binary mismatch (built for CUDA 11.8) vs runtime driver/CUDA 12.1 -> leads to allocator inconsistencies and sporadic OOMs. The warning supports this.
- Hypothesis B: Driver update introduced GPU hangs (NVRM Xid 79), causing memory accounting to be off or failure to free memory from crashed kernels.
- Hypothesis C: Workload increased token lengths + batching; prefetching + kv-cache + quantized model memory peaks exceed available (edge case under bursts).
- Hypothesis D: cuDNN mismatch (libcudnn version mismatch) triggers fallback codepaths that allocate more pinned memory leading to OOM. Error snippet about CUDNN_8.7 missing supports version mismatch on some nodes.

What I've tried as quick mitigations (results):
- Pinning PyTorch to a CUDA 12.1 wheel (nightly) in a local image: reduced OOMs in local repro runs but not fully eliminated under high concurrency.
- Rolling back node driver to 535.x on a small canary subset: OOMs dropped to near-0 for that subset (promising).
- Lowering dynamic batch max size from 8 -> 4: reduced peak memory; latency increased slightly; error rate lowered in load tests.
- Disabled KV-cache for long-context requests in the canary: reduced OOM frequency but broke correctness for some routes (not acceptable broadly).
- Set TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 which reduced fragmentation in some runs, helped a bit.

Data collected / debugging artifacts (local):
- torch.cuda.memory_summary() outputs (attached as text snippets in ticket).
- nvidia-smi logs (sampling every 1s) showing memory/time of OOM events.
- kernel NVRM logs at time of crash.

Next steps / proposed plan:
1) Fleet-level: Roll back driver to 535.x as emergency mitigation for Dedicated fleet until we can validate PyTorch/CUDA 12 compat end-to-end. Coordinate with infra change window.
2) Engineering: Build a canary image with PyTorch built for CUDA 12.1 (or use official wheel for 12.1) and run sustained load tests on canary fleet for 72h. Track OOMs and Xid events.
3) Runtime: Add a guard in dynamic batching for request length -> enforce stricter max batch size if sequence_len > 8k. Configurable SLO toggle.
4) Investigate cuDNN versions across images: ensure libcudnn.so version consistent with drivers and PyTorch expectations. Rebuild images with pinned cudnn 8.9/8.7 as appropriate.
5) Add better telemetry: log torch.cuda.memory_allocated/reserved per request id, and emit alerts when fragmentation > threshold.

Notes to self / gotchas:
- PyTorch's cuda version string (torch.version.cuda) reflects build target, not runtime driver. Need to check both.
- Xid 79 often correlates with GPU hangs; driver rollback reduced these on canary.
- Quantized models can have different memory patterns; 4-bit reduces model params but increases temp buffer usage in some kernels.
- Avoid quick global fleet changes; prefer small canaries with heavy load and long runs.

Tickets / links:
- JIRA-2048: "Dedicated fleet intermittent GPU OOMs after driver upgrade" (owner: infra)
- Github PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/512 (adds memory telemetry hooks)
- Confluence doc: serving-runtime/gpu-oom-troubleshooting (working draft)

Open questions / items to verify:
- Do we have a validated PyTorch wheel for CUDA 12.1 that matches our distro? If not, build+test.
- Are there any kernel driver bugs between 560.x and our AMI/kernel version that cause Xid 79? Check NVIDIA release notes and kernel compatibility.
- Can we implement per-request preflight memory estimation (cheap heuristic) to reject expensive combos instead of letting runtime OOM?

Quick commands to reproduce locally (copyable):
- docker run --gpus all -it --rm -v $(pwd)/model:/model prod-like-image:canary /bin/bash
- python repro/run_batch_infer.py --model /model/7b-4bit --batch 8 --seq_len 12000 --concurrency 50
- watch -n1 nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total,utilization.gpu --format=csv

If anything else occurs I'll paste additional logs here.

-- Anna
